message.content: Painting the Eiffel Tower isn’t a quick weekend job – it’s a major engineering and logistics effort. In practice the tower is repainted roughly every 7–8 years as part of its routine maintenance program. Each repainting cycle typically lasts a few months (often 2–3 months) once crews are on site, but the whole operation—from preparation and scaffolding to the final coat—requires careful planning, safety protocols, and coordination with the city’s heritage authorities. So while the actual “painting” phase might span a couple of months, the overall project from start to finish can extend over a longer period depending on weather, crew size, and logistical constraints.
